name: Unikraft Cloud

modes.label: Self-serve plan pool (Hobby / Team / Pro concurrent running capacity)
modes.commit_note: Flat monthly plan; pool = concurrent RUNNING capacity. Scaled-to-zero (standby) instances do not consume it (Hobby 5 / Team 50 / Pro 5,000 standby). Pool month equals the plan fee (plans carry fee_is_credit=true so the fee is not charged twice).
modes.note: No metered rate or overage published; exceeding the running pool is presumably blocked by quota (unverified). Per-instance max RAM 8 GiB taken from the quotas-doc example account (not a published plan limit). A 4 vCPU / 8 GiB instance fits 1x on Team and 4x on Pro (memory-bound), none on Hobby.

modes.label: Enterprise: dedicated hosts / on-prem / BYOC (custom price)
modes.note: Unlimited instances, dedicated host fleet, on-prem/BYOC, named SRE, 1 h SLA. Enterprise-only: GPU preview (1 NVIDIA GPU/instance, QEMU 'full' VMs), arm64 hosts, nested virtualization, network shield (egress filtering + secret injection), sandbox plugin (exec/filesystem API). Customer story cites ~$0.30/h per browser at bare-metal economics (customer-reported, not a list price).

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Free forever, no card. 2 running instances (2 vCPU / 4 GiB total), 5 standby (8 GiB standby storage), 10 GiB image storage.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $39/mo buys the Team pool (8 running instances, 8 vCPU / 8 GiB total), 50 standby (15 GiB), 50 GiB images, transparent migration. fee_is_credit=true only to avoid double-counting the identical pool tier price.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $199/mo buys the Pro pool (24 running instances, 24 vCPU / 32 GiB total), 5,000 standby (1 TiB standby storage), 100 GiB images, user-defined proxy, snapshot history & rollback, live kernel updates, priority support.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing; unlimited instances; dedicated hosts, on-prem/BYOC; SOC2/HIPAA/audit logs; 1 h SLA.

caveats: Unikraft Cloud publishes NO per-hour, per-GiB or egress price: self-serve pricing is a flat plan fee that caps concurrent running capacity (Hobby 2 vCPU/4 GiB/2 instances, Team 8 vCPU/8 GiB/8, Pro 24 vCPU/32 GiB/24). Anything bigger is Enterprise (custom price). Modelled as a pool mode.

Idle cost is $0 by design: scale-to-zero puts instances in standby in ~ms (stateful mode snapshots memory to disk) and standby instances don't count toward the running pool; standby storage included (8 GiB / 15 GiB / 1 TiB).

Self-serve sandbox ergonomics are limited: the sandbox plugin (command exec + filesystem API used by the JS SDK Sandbox class), network shield egress filtering, GPUs, arm64 and nested virtualization are Enterprise-only; instance forking is preview. Self-serve users deploy Dockerfile images as HTTP/TLS services.
Per-instance max vCPU/RAM per plan unpublished; max_ram_gib 8 comes from the quotas doc example (1 vCPU max there). The pool tiers may therefore overstate what a single instance can get.
Whether running above plan capacity is blocked or billed is not documented (no overage prices).
Egress/bandwidth not priced or capped on the pricing page; network values null.
snapshot_gib_month 0 = standby storage included within plan quota; no price for going beyond the quota.
Claimed <10 ms cold start / scale-to-zero is a vendor figure; no independent benchmark (perf null).
Regions: dal, fra, sfo, sin, was metros; 28 more listed as potential on request.
open_source=false for the platform; CLI/kraftkit/Terraform provider are open source (and the separate unikraft.org unikernel project).
Launched 2024-04-02 as KraftCloud (Launch HN, closed beta); rebranded Unikraft Cloud; domain now unikraft.com.

Re-checked 2026-09-28 (unikraft.com/pricing rendered in headless Chrome, unikraft.com/llms-full.txt): still no pay-as-you-go / per-instance / per-vCPU-hour rate; self-serve is only Hobby $0 / Team $39 / Pro $199 flat plans plus Enterprise custom. No PAYG regime can be carded.

fleet.tiers: Hobby 2 live/2 vCPU/4 GiB; Team 8 live/8 vCPU/8 GiB; Pro 24 live/24 vCPU/32 GiB; Enterprise custom. Standby 5/50/5,000 separately.
fleet.notes: All resource-pool caps apply together. 10 lightweight running instances need Pro; 50/300/1,000 running need Enterprise, even though 5,000 standby fit Pro. At 4 vCPU/8 GiB Pro holds only 4 by RAM. No quota approval SLA.

snapshot_auto.quote: With stateful scale-to-zero Unikraft Cloud takes a [snapshot](/features/snapshots) of the instance state before putting it into standby.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in (--scale-to-zero policy=on,stateful=true). Triggered when the instance idles into standby (no TCP/HTTP traffic for the cooldown); memory included, restored lazily on wake by the next request/packet. An explicit stop does NOT snapshot (stopped instances unmount volumes). Scheduled checkpoints via cron-style scheduled operations also exist.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A **checkpoint** captures the full state of an instance—its memory and volume state—at any moment, so you can later start new instances that resume from exactly that state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory + volumes; taken from a running instance (pauses only a few ms, CoW); new instances boot from it, reusable many times; checkpoint history/rollback. Also branching (clone a live instance) and instance templates. Snapshot history & rollback listed as a Pro-plan feature.

harness_api.quote: The sandbox plugin lets you run commands and manipulate the filesystem inside an instance, over the plugin endpoint
harness_api.note: Only a generic exec/filesystem sandbox plugin (Enterprise); no API to drive Claude Code/Codex/etc. found in docs.

ingress_rules.quote: To connect to an instance from the Internet, you need to create a service and attach the instance to it.
ingress_rules.note: Instances are private by default (private IP + <name>.internal FQDN); a service maps chosen external FQDN ports to internal ports (TLS mandatory). Tunnel command for private access. No IP allowlist / auth on public URLs documented; plugin endpoints are authenticated.

volume_attach.quote: A volume is a persistent storage device that keeps data across restarts and even redeployments.
volume_attach.note: Block (ext4) volumes created/attached/detached via API/CLI/SDK; attach to running instance applies on next scale-to-zero cycle.

volume_shared.quote: `rwx`       | Read-write many. The volume can be mounted in read-write mode by multiple instances simultaneously. This access mode is only supported for volumes with `virtiofs` filesystem.
volume_shared.note: Read-write many via virtiofs volumes (slower than block); rox = read-only many for block volumes. BYOC/on-prem can add custom filesystem drivers (e.g. S3 via JuiceFS); managed host-path volumes Enterprise.

docker_inside.quote: Why can't you just use a container? When you deploy a container on the public cloud, it gets deployed on top of a virtual machine to have strong, hardware-level isolation... At Unikraft, Dockerfiles create the filesystem at build time. Then, a lean microVM provides the best efficiency at deploy time.
docker_inside.note: Unikraft turns your Dockerfile into the microVM image itself at build time (TinyX); the running instance is a minimal Linux microVM, not a host with a Docker/OCI container runtime inside it. nested_virt is also false in the card (no /dev/kvm), and no docs mention running docker/containerd inside a running instance.

anti_bot.quote: Unikraft Cloud (unikraft.com) runs any Dockerfile-based workload as a minimal, Linux-based microVM with hardware-level isolation, sub-10ms cold starts, millisecond scale-to-zero, and 100,000+ strongly isolated instances per server.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Unikraft Cloud is a general-purpose compute/microVM platform (customers run their own Chrome/browser workloads on it, e.g. Browser Use); it does not itself provide stealth/anti-fingerprinting for bot detection.

captcha_solving.quote: Unikraft Cloud (unikraft.com) runs any Dockerfile-based workload as a minimal, Linux-based microVM with hardware-level isolation, sub-10ms cold starts, millisecond scale-to-zero, and 100,000+ strongly isolated instances per server.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. It is infrastructure (microVMs) for running any workload, not a browser/automation product with built-in CAPTCHA solving.

live_resize.quote: Resize instance memory: unikraft instance edit demo-instance --memory 256 ... --vcpus n Number of vCPUs.
live_resize.note: `unikraft instance edit` can change --memory and --vcpus on an existing instance via `--set`/flags without recreating it.

own_agent_api.quote: Run millions of agents and functions on just a few servers -- not a datacenter.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Unikraft Cloud provides microVM compute for AI workloads (including running other companies' agents), but ships no first-party API that drives its OWN browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: Repos: cli, cpp-sdk, docs, examples, go-sdk, harbor, js-sdk, k8s-operator, lib-ukp-bin, openapi, pg_ukc_scaletozero, plugin-sdk, python-sdk, tailscale, terraform-provider-ukc, unikraft-videos, x
mcp_server.note: No MCP-server repository in the unikraft-cloud GitHub org, and no MCP mention in docs/llms-full.txt; the platform ships CLI + JS/Python/Go/C++ SDKs + Terraform provider + K8s operator instead.

lang_python.quote: runtime: python:3.12 ... The runtime specifies one of the Unikraft Cloud runtimes (microVMs) built to run different languages and apps. Here it specifies a Python runtime.
lang_python.note: Official python:3.x runtime plus a Python HTTP-server guide (/guides/httpserver-python3.12) and a first-party async Python SDK (unikraft-cloud, Python 3.10+).

lang_node.quote: `@unikraft/cloud` for Node.js and TypeScript. Fully typed, with chainable handles, multi-metro fan-out, and a `Sandbox` class for running commands and moving files inside an instance.
lang_node.note: Official Node.js/TypeScript SDK plus Node runtime guides (Node HTTP Server, Express, Next.js, etc. under /guides).

secret_proxy.quote: The shield provides filtering capabilities but also the possibility to inject credentials/secrets for agentic or other use cases. This is useful in sandbox environments, as it means the sandbox won't need unfiltered network access or access to secrets.
secret_proxy.note: Network shield relay microVM sits in front of the workload and can inject credentials for third-party APIs/package registries generically (any-http), not just model-provider keys. Currently Enterprise-only ('Limited Access' preview); also matches the Browser Use customer story pattern (control-plane proxy holds all credentials).

max_session_h.quote: vcpu limit: 1-1 ... memory size limits: 16MiB-8GiB ... autoscale limit: 0-16
max_session_h.note: Quotas doc only caps concurrency/size, not wall-clock duration; instances are VM-style (running until stopped, or scaled to standby on idle via wake_on_request/auto_stop_idle), with no published maximum session length.

nested_virt.quote: An instance can now reach the host's virtualization extensions, so a hypervisor runs inside the guest. Request the feature per instance with the new `nested-virt` feature flag ... Requires the new `nested_virt` user permission, and the host must carry a nested virtualization configuration. ... **Enterprise only.**
nested_virt.note: Shipped in Release 13 (2026-09-02), Enterprise-only (permission-gated). Card's enterprise-dedicated mode already lists nested_virt:true; the top-level features.nested_virt should also be true since the feature is genuinely offered (paid tier), matching how gpu/arm64 are treated.

ssh.quote: Coming soon: SSH directly into an instance, create and delete instances, and inspect the lifetime of an instance as you checkpoint or fork it — among other things.
ssh.note: Still listed as 'coming soon' as of Release 11 and never mentioned as shipped in the later R12/R13 release notes or current docs (no /guides/ssh page exists, 404). Access today is via the exec/filesystem sandbox plugin (Enterprise) or the CLI/API, not SSH.

desktop.quote: Unikraft Cloud runs workloads on minimal, Linux-based microVMs ... It runs any Docker-based workload
desktop.note: Unikraft Cloud is an infrastructure platform for running any Dockerfile-based workload (incl. customer-run headless browsers) as a microVM; it does not itself offer a graphical desktop (VNC/RDP/stream) product. Plainly outside the product.

browser.quote:
### Browser Workloads
Isolated sessions cold started in < 10 ms
browser.note: Customers (Kernel, Tinyfish, Browser Use) run their own headless browsers inside microVMs; Unikraft Cloud itself does not manage/provide a browser as a first-party feature — only the infra to host one from a Dockerfile.

computer_use.quote: The sandbox plugin lets you run commands and manipulate the filesystem inside an instance, over the plugin endpoint
computer_use.note: No screenshot+click driving API found anywhere in docs; the only control-plane API is the generic exec/filesystem sandbox plugin (Enterprise). Plainly not offered.

agent_harnesses.quote:
### AI Agents
Spawn and scale 1000+ agents in seconds
agent_harnesses.note: The AI page markets running agent workloads (bring-your-own-Dockerfile), but no preinstalled coding-agent templates (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) are documented anywhere on the site or in the CLI/API docs.

egress_allowlist.quote: Network shield and relay is a new feature which is available to enterprise customers. ... The shield provides filtering capabilities but also the possibility to inject credentials/secrets for agentic or other use cases.
egress_allowlist.note: The network shield is an Enterprise-only microVM that sits between an instance and the internet and filters outbound traffic (plus secret injection), matching the definition of egress_allowlist. Genuinely offered, so should be true, consistent with the card's enterprise-dedicated mode which already lists egress_allowlist:true.

public_ipv4.quote: Every instance, by default, receives a private IP and a private FQDN (of the format `<instance-name>.internal`).
public_ipv4.note: Public reachability is via a service's public FQDN behind Unikraft's own load balancer/proxy (TLS), not a per-instance public IPv4 address; no public IPv4 allocation is documented anywhere.

gpu.quote: Release 12 introduces GPU support for enterprise customers ... The platform now supports NVIDIA GPUs. You select the instance type and GPU count when creating an instance via `POST /v1/instances` ... Requires instance `type` `full` and a plan with GPU support.
gpu.note: GPU instances (NVIDIA, via full-VM type) are a real, shipped, Enterprise-only feature, consistent with the card's own enterprise-dedicated mode (gpu:true) and note about the GPU preview / browser customer story. Should be true at top level too.

windows.quote: Unikraft Cloud runs workloads on minimal, Linux-based microVMs ... It provides VM-level isolation, not container-level isolation.
windows.note: The platform only runs Linux-based microVMs/full VMs; no Windows guest OS is offered anywhere in docs, pricing, or release notes. (The CLI tool itself also isn't officially supported on native Windows, only via WSL, per the FAQ — a separate, corroborating point.)

macos.quote: Unikraft Cloud runs workloads on minimal, Linux-based microVMs
macos.note: Linux-only guest platform; no macOS machines offered anywhere in docs, pricing, or release notes.

arm64.quote: Both `x86_64` and `arm64`, and the hosted platform runs on `x86_64`. ... `arm64` hosts are available as part of enterprise plans. To deploy to them, reach out to the Unikraft Cloud Discord or send an email to support@unikraft.com.
arm64.note: ARM64 host support shipped in Release 13 (2026-09-02) and is real, documented, and orderable (Enterprise-only). Should be true, matching the card's own enterprise-dedicated mode (arm64:true).

open_source.quote: Unikraft Cloud (unikraft.com) is the commercial cloud platform built by Unikraft Inc. It must NOT be confused with: - The open-source Unikraft unikernel project at unikraft.org (a Linux Foundation project)
open_source.note: The Unikraft Cloud platform itself (controller, proxy, dashboard, API) is closed-source/commercial. Only the `unikraft` CLI ('the open source `unikraft` CLI tool', per docs/faq.md) and the unrelated unikraft.org unikernel project are open source — the core product is not.

egress_ip_type.quote: Every instance, by default, receives a private IP and a private FQDN (of the format `<instance-name>.internal`).
egress_ip_type.note: Unikraft Cloud is a bare-metal/microVM cloud platform running out of its own datacenter metros (dal, fra, sfo, sin, was, etc.); instances have no public IPv4 and reach the internet only through Unikraft's own load balancer / network shield infrastructure, i.e. ordinary datacenter egress IPs (not residential/mobile). No page enumerates the egress ranges explicitly, hence medium confidence.

static_egress_ip.quote: The shield provides filtering capabilities but also the possibility to inject credentials/secrets for agentic or other use cases. This is useful in sandbox environments, as it means the sandbox won't need unfiltered network access or access to secrets.
static_egress_ip.note: No feature is documented anywhere (pricing, docs, release notes, FAQ) for allocating a fixed/static outbound IP per instance or per account; the only egress-shaping feature is the Enterprise-only 'network shield' relay microVM, which filters/injects credentials but is never described as providing a stable/static egress IP address. Treated as not offered.

sso.quote: Use one of the sign-in methods below to continue. Continue with GitHub / Continue with Google
sso.note: The console only offers GitHub/Google OAuth sign-in; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO is documented on the pricing page (even the Enterprise tier's listed extras are 'Dedicated host fleet, On-prem / BYOC deploy, SOC2 · HIPAA · audit logs, Named SRE · 1h SLA' with no SSO mention) or anywhere else on the site/docs.

usage_api.quote: Unikraft Cloud publishes NO per-hour, per-GiB or egress price: self-serve pricing is a flat plan fee that caps concurrent running capacity (Hobby 2 vCPU/4 GiB/2 instances, Team 8 vCPU/8 GiB/8, Pro 24 vCPU/32 GiB/24). Anything bigger is Enterprise (custom price).
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Billing is pooled (flat monthly fee, no per-sandbox metering). No API documented for retrieving per-sandbox usage/cost. Instances are metered only at the account level as part of the plan's running capacity limits.

locations_quote: By default, at present, Unikraft Cloud supports the following metros: dal (Dallas, TX, USA), fra (Frankfurt, DE), sfo (San Francisco, USA), sin (Singapore), was (Washington DC, USA).
